clue.text: Mate imprisons Romeo, one involved in second city disgrace

indicators.note: the mate holds the Romeo letter captive, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an oppo is British slang for a mate or colleague
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: being involved in something here means being placed within it

parts.note: Brum is Birmingham, often called Britain's second city
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A friend jails a lover, and a scandal unfolds in Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is the informal name for Birmingham, England's second-largest city.
explanation.definitionFit: Opprobrium is public shame or harsh criticism, a synonym for disgrace.

clue.text: Curse characters in Number 10

indicators.note: only some letters inside the answer to another clue are kept, the outer ones dropped

parts.note: the answer to clue 10, which is the word loathsome

explanation.surface: Swearing goes on inside Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' reads as the Prime Minister's residence at 10 Downing Street, but it points to the answer to 10 Across, LOATHSOME, which holds OATH.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath can be a swear word, so it is a curse in the profanity sense.

clue.text: Perhaps hippo suffering cramp around London Park

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap themselves round the park
the word cramp is in a bad way, so its letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: Hyde Park is a large royal park in central London

explanation.surface: A hippo at the zoo in a London park is struck by cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges the cramp letters to PACRM, which split to go 'around' the park; 'Perhaps' warns the hippo is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pachyderm is a thick-skinned large mammal, and the hippopotamus is an example.

clue.text: Nothing unchanged for Nineties band

parts.note: O looks like zero, meaning nothing
as is means left just as it was, unchanged

explanation.surface: A Nineties group whose sound never changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis were a Manchester rock group famous in the Britpop era of the 1990s.

clue.text: With bread, soak up fish dish

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
to mop is to soak up liquid with a cloth or sponge

explanation.surface: Use bread to wipe up the sauce of a fish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled around a filling, served as a dish.

clue.text: Without prompting, king enters nude, as eccentric

indicators.note: the king goes in among the other letters, so one piece sits inside another
odd or off-centre, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch walks in naked, quite unbidden, which is rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram ('eccentric') of NUDE AS gives UNASED, and K 'enters' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unasked is done without being requested, so without prompting.

clue.text: Inflame edge of gum and tooth

parts.note: to fan flames or passions is to inflame them

indicators.note: the edge here is the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Something irritates the gum line next to a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long pointed tooth, as of a dog or snake.

clue.text: In telegram, orator raised stink

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read from bottom to top, backwards
the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A speaker kicked up a fuss in a telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: AMORA lies 'In' telegrAM ORAtor and is 'raised', read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell; here used neutrally for a stink, as any odour.

clue.text: Brains evicting unruly civilians from matinee Virgil Tracy's mishandled

indicators.note: throwing out, so these letters are removed from the larger pool
disorderly, so the removed letters need not be in their printed order
badly handled, so what remains of the pool is rearranged

parts.note: the pool of letters to work from
the letters to be taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Virgil Tracy of Thunderbirds bungles throwing rowdy civilians out of a matinee.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: the letters of MATINEE VIRGIL TRACYS, less those of CIVILIANS ('evicting unruly'), are 'mishandled' to give the answer. Virgil Tracy is a pilot in the puppet TV show Thunderbirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey matter is informal for the brain's tissue, and so for intelligence or brains.

clue.text: Pet turns over bone in food from Mexico

indicators.note: flipping round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet
os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone

explanation.surface: A pet flips a bone into its Mexican dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacos are folded tortillas with fillings, a staple of Mexican cuisine.

clue.text: Vile student has MeToo upset

parts.note: L is for learner, the student driver's plate

indicators.note: knocked over, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A student is upset by the MeToo movement, finding it vile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the student's feelings, but it signals rearranging the next words' letters into OATHSOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathsome means arousing disgust or hatred, a synonym of vile.

clue.text: Leader placed cans

parts.note: a head is a leader, as of a school or department
set means put or placed

explanation.surface: A boss has put down tins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cans' looks like tins, but it is slang for headphones.
explanation.definitionFit: Cans is slang for headphones, and a headset is a pair of headphones.

clue.text: Gossip involves terrible sham means of covering up

indicators.note: to involve here is to enfold, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to yak is to chatter or gossip

indicators.note: dreadful, so the letters of this word are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Gossips spread a dreadful lie about a cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram ('terrible') of SHAM gives ASHM, which YAK 'involves'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women to hide the face in public.

clue.text: Fear god coming in in the morning

indicators.note: entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a.m. abbreviates ante meridiem, before noon
Lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: Someone dreads a deity turning up at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lares were Roman guardian gods of the home; one of them is a Lar.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fright or apprehension, a synonym of fear.

clue.text: Hesitate about working party producing pointless work

indicators.note: around, so the hesitating word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to boggle is to hesitate or shy at something
on means operating, working
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: Someone dithers over a works party that is a waste of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A boondoggle is American slang for wasteful, unnecessary work or a pointless project.

clue.text: Coincide with friend coming back after some cricket

indicators.note: the friend piece follows the cricket piece in the answer

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket

indicators.note: returning, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Meet up with a mate who's back after a spell of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlap is to partly coincide, sharing time or space.

clue.text: Cuckoo touched nuts and crackers

definitions.meaning: crackers is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone eccentric touched the nuts and crackers on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Four definitions in a row, each meaning mad; the surface suggests a party snack table.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic is a mad person, and as an adjective it means crazy, like each word.

clue.text: O'Connor perhaps is unable to provide accompaniment

parts.note: Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: A singer called O'Connor can't supply the backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Des O'Connor was a long-running British television host and crooner.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung or played above the main tune, an accompaniment.

clue.text: Flat tyre's front supports separate pieces

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece lies below the others

parts.note: apart means separate
chessmen and draughtsmen are pieces, or men

indicators.note: the front is the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A flat tyre's tread props up broken bits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a punctured tyre, but it is the home.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat in British usage is an apartment, a set of rooms on one floor.

clue.text: Candidate in vote against source of coal energy

parts.note: a no is a vote against
a mine is where coal comes from
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A candidate votes against coal and energy policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for an office or award, so a candidate.

clue.text: Cycling family in time before reservation

indicators.note: the cycled family goes inside the time piece

parts.note: eve means evening, a time

indicators.note: going round, so the first letter moves to the end

parts.note: a clan is a family group

explanation.surface: A family goes cycling in the evening before reaching a reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves the last letter of CLAN to the front, giving NCLA, which goes 'in' EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory surrounded by another, like a reservation set apart.

clue.text: Pervert Frenchman's quick to seize Spanish aunt

indicators.note: grabbing hold, so the aunt is held inside

parts.note: vite is French for quick
tía is Spanish for aunt

explanation.surface: A fast Frenchman grabs a Spanish aunt, a perverted act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' looks like a noun for a person, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitiate is to corrupt or debase, which is to pervert something.

clue.text: Five of us oddly dear to French guarantor

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: only the first, third and so on letters are kept

parts.note: cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: Five of us, strangely fond of the French, stand as guarantors.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher is a document that vouches for something, a guarantor of value.

clue.text: Set of eight books about cold empty economist

indicators.note: around, so the books piece wraps the cold piece

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: with its contents gone, only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A shelf of books about a dull economist.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, such as eight musicians.

clue.text: Carry motorway sign

parts.note: to tote is to carry
M is used for UK motorway names like the M1

explanation.surface: Someone lugs a motorway sign about.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem or symbol, a sign standing for a group.

clue.text: Overthrow permitted for two

parts.note: a coup is an overthrow of a government
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Two people were allowed to stage a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' is the definition: a pair of lines in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A couplet is a pair of rhyming lines, so a set of two.

clue.text: Blockage I end in diplomatic reasoning

parts.note: a log jam is a blockage, so log stands for it

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A deadlock ends in diplomatic reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the system of sound argument, which is reasoning.

clue.text: Almost perfect plan

indicators.note: nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A near-perfect plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a scheme or intention, so a plan.

clue.text: Enter without payment: takings collapse

parts.note: the gate is the money taken from spectators at a match
a crash is a collapse, as of markets

explanation.surface: Getting in for free makes the box-office takings collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to go to a party or event uninvited, without paying.

clue.text: Yes, American's lacking in gluttony

indicators.note: missing, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: agreed is a way of saying yes
A is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Yes, Americans are short on gluttony.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is an excessive desire, and gluttony is greed for food.

clue.text: Landmines literally in trees

parts.note: read as L and Ms, the letter names el and ems spoken

explanation.surface: Explosives planted among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' says to treat Landmines as letters: L and M's, which said as letter names run el-ems.
explanation.definitionFit: Elms are large deciduous trees of the genus Ulmus.

clue.text: Arranged to cart a tree, mostly chestnut

indicators.note: set in a new order, so these letters are rearranged
most of the word, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone organises carting a chestnut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: TRE is TREE less its last letter ('mostly'); 'Arranged' shuffles TOCARTA with TRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is a brownish-orange colour, close to chestnut.
